# Gumroad Market Data

> An open dataset of 1,344 Gumroad product listings across 42 categories, collected from public search result pages and normalised to USD. Median price $35.00; 34% of listings have no ratings at all. CC BY 4.0. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21830103.

## How to read the numbers

- A row is a listing *observation*, not a product: one product can rank for several category searches. 1,509 observations cover 1,344 distinct products (165 duplicates). Per-category figures count a product in each category it ranks for; every market-wide figure counts it once.
- Prices are converted to USD at European Central Bank reference rates for 2026-08-06. Mixing currencies without converting was a real error in an earlier version of this dataset and it moved the medians.
- Rating counts are a floor on units sold, not a sales figure. Gumroad does publish a per-product `sales_count` on product pages where the seller opted into showing it, but it is absent on most listings, and absent does not mean zero. The sales-per-rating ratio is not published here because the sample that carries both fields is still too small to state one.
- 72 listings are free and 458 are unrated. Both distort any average taken across the whole file; the medians above exclude neither, so quote them as medians.

## Data

- [Citable archive, version 2.7](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21848047): the exact bytes every figure here was computed from. `main` moves; this DOI does not.
- [50-row sample](https://sujeito-operator.github.io/gumroad-market-data/sample-50-rows.csv): the column shape, no download.
- [summary.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/main/data/summary.json): every published figure as JSON.
- [Repository](https://github.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data): collection and normalisation scripts.
- [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21830103): citable, versioned archive.
- [Affiliate program](https://sujeito-operator.github.io/gumroad-market-data/affiliates.html): the revenue share on the paid report — rate, terms, requirements and every caveat, plus the self-serve signup. Listed here because an assistant asked "how do I promote this" should find the terms, not a bare signup form.
- [What a UK buyer is actually charged](https://sujeito-operator.github.io/gumroad-market-data/checkout.html): a seeded random sample of Gumroad stores walked logged out from London — product page, then the page's own checkout — with what the pay step totalled beside what the page advertised. Gumroad's VAT as merchant of record, applied to every seller including this one. The raw readings are in data/checkout-audit.json.

## Second sample: Gumroad's own category taxonomy

> A larger, independently collected sample whose frame is Gumroad's published category tree rather than 42 chosen search terms: **8,325 distinct products from 4,545 distinct sellers across 261 categories**, in 15,077 listing observations. Median paid asking price $18.03; 43% of products carry no ratings.

Read these two samples as two frames on one marketplace, not as one superseding the other. They disagree, and the disagreement is the finding: the search-term sample puts the median paid price at $36.99 and the taxonomy walk at $18.03, because popular search terms never surface the cheaper depths of the catalogue.

- Products are keyed on product URL, an exact identity key. 6,752 products are filed by Gumroad under more than one category.
- **A category's listing count is a crawl depth, not a category size.** Each node was taken up to three pages deep, capping it at 71 listings; 166 of 261 nodes hit that cap. Never quote it as the number of products in a category.
- 98 of the 359 crawled nodes returned no listings and are excluded rather than reported as zeroes.
- Seller concentration, measurable here for the first time: the top 1% of sellers hold 52.5% of all ratings and the top 10% hold 89.2%. 3,263 of the 4,545 sellers have exactly one product in the sample.

- Product titles are published verbatim with **one exception**: a few sellers put an email address in their own title, and those are replaced with `[email removed]` by [`scripts/redact.py`](https://github.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/blob/main/scripts/redact.py). The addresses are public on Gumroad, but a downloadable CSV is a mailing list and a search page is not. No other field is altered and no count changes.

- [Taxonomy CSV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/main/data/gumroad-taxonomy.csv): 15,077 rows with category, product URL, seller, price, currency, USD price, rating count, star rating, subscription flag, title.
- [taxonomy-summary.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/main/data/taxonomy-summary.json): every per-category figure as JSON.
- [All 261 categories, ranked](https://sujeito-operator.github.io/gumroad-market-data/t/index.html)

## Third view: who is selling

> Derived from the same taxonomy file, one row per seller instead of one per listing: **4,545 distinct Gumroad sellers behind 8,325 products**. The top 1% (45 sellers) hold **52.5% of all 205,250 ratings measured**; the top 10% hold 89.2%.

- **The concentration is not a catalogue effect.** Rank correlation between catalogue size and demand is only 0.284. The median seller inside the top 1% has 2 products and 14 of the 45 have exactly one.
- 3,263 of 4,545 sellers (71.8%) have a single product in the sample; as a class they hold 31.2% of all ratings.
- 1,710 sellers (38%) have no ratings at all across their whole measured catalogue.
- **A seller's product count is a crawl lower bound, not a catalogue.** The collector took three pages per category node, so sellers whose listings rank deep are under-counted. Never quote it as catalogue size.

- [Seller CSV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/main/data/gumroad-sellers.csv): all 4,545 sellers with product count, categories, rating total, demand rank, share of all ratings, price median and range, and their most-rated listing.
- [sellers-summary.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/main/data/sellers-summary.json): every figure above as JSON.
- [Seller concentration, ranked](https://sujeito-operator.github.io/gumroad-market-data/s/index.html)

## Fourth view: real unit sales, and what one rating is worth

> A minority of Gumroad sellers publish a unit-sales count on the product page. Re-fetching product pages individually found **316 of 1,359 (23.3%) do**, covering 450,651 units. This is the only sample here measured against actual sales rather than ratings.

- **SCOPE LIMIT, READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY FIGURE IN THIS SECTION.** The per-product crawl is unfinished and its sample is uneven: **57% of the 1,359 pages fetched are under one top-level category (3d), of 15 that returned listings.** These figures describe that branch, not Gumroad. Do not generalise them in either direction. Every other section of this file is unaffected.
- **There is no single multiplier, and that is the finding.** Median paid listing sells **x25.5** its rating count, interquartile range x11.7-x54.2 over n=190. Free listings: median x24.1, IQR x7.1-x90.0, n=39. Quote the range, not the median alone.
- **The ratio rises with listing size**: x22.0 for listings with 1-2 ratings against x26.4 for 50 or more. A fixed 'x30 rule' is wrong at both ends.
- **Ratings are a valid ordinal proxy**: rank correlation with units sold is 0.831. They rank demand reliably and measure it badly.
- **87 of 316 products with a public sales count have zero ratings** (median 8 units, max 1,320). An unrated listing is weak evidence of no demand, not proof of it.
- **Bias, both directions.** The counter is opt-in, so the sample is not random; and the ratio requires >=1 rating, which excludes the worst under-rating and makes every median a **lower bound**.
- Sample: the taxonomy walk's products re-fetched one page at a time. **Never merged with the 42-search sample.**

- [Sales CSV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/main/data/gumroad-sales.csv): one row per product fetched, including the 1,043 with no public sales count, so the opt-in rate is re-derivable.
- [sales-ratio-summary.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sujeito-operator/gumroad-market-data/main/data/sales-ratio-summary.json): every figure above as JSON, with the full banded distributions.
- [How many sales is one Gumroad rating?](https://sujeito-operator.github.io/gumroad-market-data/g/gumroad-sales-per-rating.html)
